title: OLYMPIAD SCIENCE — Chemistry | Natural Products
description: Subject-wise test on Natural Products (Chemistry) for OLYMPIAD SCIENCE. 15Q.
subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following natural products is classified as an alkaloid?

options.explanation: Cellulose is a polysaccharide.
Insulin is a protein hormone.
Morphine is a well-known alkaloid derived from the opium poppy.
Cholesterol is a steroid.

questions.explanation: Morphine is a well-known alkaloid derived from the opium poppy, characterized by the presence of nitrogen atoms in its structure. Cellulose is a polysaccharide, insulin is a protein hormone, and cholesterol is a steroid.
questions.subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: The terpene limonene, commonly found in citrus fruits, has which of the following structural features?

options.explanation: Limonene does not have a fused ring system.

options.text: A six-membered ring with alternating double bonds
options.explanation: Limonene does not have alternating double bonds.

options.text: A single six-membered ring with one double bond and two methyl groups
options.explanation: Limonene is a monocyclic terpene with a six-membered ring containing one double bond and two methyl substituents.

options.text: A linear chain of 15 carbon atoms
options.explanation: Limonene does not have a 15-carbon linear chain.

questions.explanation: Limonene is a monocyclic terpene with a six-membered ring containing one double bond and two methyl substituents.
questions.subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about the antibiotic penicillin?

options.text: It contains a β-lactam ring fused to a five-membered thiazolidine ring
options.explanation: Penicillin contains a β-lactam ring fused to a five-membered thiazolidine ring.

options.text: It is produced by the fungus Aspergillus niger
options.explanation: Penicillin is produced by Penicillium fungi, not Aspergillus.

options.text: It is a broad-spectrum antibiotic effective against viruses
options.explanation: Penicillin is ineffective against viruses.

options.text: It is a polyketide derived from amino acids
options.explanation: Penicillin is not a polyketide but a non-ribosomal peptide.

questions.explanation: Penicillin contains a β-lactam ring fused to a five-membered thiazolidine ring, which is essential for its antibacterial activity.
questions.subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: The natural pigment chlorophyll differs from heme in that chlorophyll contains:

options.text: A porphyrin ring with Fe²⁺ at its center
options.explanation: Chlorophyll does not have a porphyrin ring with Fe²⁺.

options.text: A chlorin ring and a phytol tail
options.explanation: Chlorophyll contains a chlorin ring and a phytol tail.
Chlorophyll does not have a linear tetrapyrrole structure.

options.text: A corrin ring and cobalt at its center
options.explanation: Chlorophyll does not have a corrin ring and cobalt.

questions.explanation: Chlorophyll contains a chlorin ring and a phytol tail, whereas heme has a porphyrin ring with Fe²⁺.
questions.subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following natural products is derived from the shikimic acid pathway?

options.explanation: Ascorbic acid is derived from glucose via the uronic acid pathway.
Taxol (paclitaxel) is derived from the shikimic acid pathway.
Glucose is a primary metabolite.
Testosterone is a steroid derived from the mevalonate pathway.

questions.explanation: Taxol (paclitaxel) is derived from the shikimic acid pathway, which is a key biosynthetic route for aromatic amino acids and many secondary metabolites.
questions.subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: The compound caffeine is classified as a:

options.explanation: Flavonoids are polyphenolic compounds.
Caffeine is a purine alkaloid, structurally derived from purine bases like adenine and guanine.
Tannins are polyphenolic polymers.
Phenolic glycosides are sugar conjugates of phenols.

questions.explanation: Caffeine is a purine alkaloid, structurally derived from purine bases like adenine and guanine.
questions.subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct statement about the structure of vitamin B12 (cobalamin)?

options.text: It contains a corrin ring with Co³⁺ at its center
options.explanation: Vitamin B12 contains a corrin ring with Co³⁺ at its center.

options.text: It is a water-soluble vitamin with a porphyrin ring
options.explanation: Vitamin B12 contains a corrin ring, not a porphyrin ring.

options.text: It is synthesized by plants and algae
options.explanation: Vitamin B12 is synthesized by bacteria, not plants or algae.

options.text: It contains a linear tetrapyrrole structure
options.explanation: Vitamin B12 contains a corrin ring, not a linear tetrapyrrole structure.

questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 contains a corrin ring, a reduced porphyrin-like structure, with cobalt (Co³⁺) at its center.

questions.question: The natural product quinine, used historically to treat malaria, is classified as:

options.explanation: Quinine is not a terpene.
Quinine is an isoquinoline alkaloid derived from the bark of the cinchona tree.
Quinine is not a sesquiterpene lactone.
Quinine is not a steroid glycoside.

questions.explanation: Quinine is an isoquinoline alkaloid derived from the bark of the cinchona tree.
questions.subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: Calculate the number of stereocenters in the natural product digitoxin, a cardiac glycoside.

options.explanation: Digitoxin has more than 5 stereocenters.
Digitoxin has 6 stereocenters in the aglycone part alone.
Digitoxin does not have 7 stereocenters.
Digitoxin does not have 8 stereocenters.

questions.explanation: Digitoxin has the molecular formula C41H64O13 and contains multiple chiral centers.

questions.question: Which of the following natural products is synthesized via the polyketide pathway?

options.explanation: Morphine is derived from amino acids.
Penicillin is derived from amino acids.
Tetracycline is a polyketide antibiotic synthesized via the polyketide pathway.
Insulin is a protein hormone.

questions.explanation: Tetracycline is a polyketide antibiotic synthesized by the condensation of acetate units via the polyketide pathway.
questions.subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following natural products is classified as an alkaloid and is known for its potent physiological effects, including pain relief and euphoria?

options.explanation: Quinine is an antimalarial alkaloid, but it does not have the same pain-relief effects.
Morphine is a well-known alkaloid derived from the opium poppy (Papaver somniferum) and is renowned for its analgesic properties.
Ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is a vitamin, not an alkaloid.
Caffeine is an alkaloid but is not primarily used for pain relief or euphoria in the same way as morphine.

questions.explanation: Morphine is a well-known alkaloid derived from the opium poppy (Papaver somniferum) and is renowned for its analgesic properties.
questions.subject: olympiad-sci-chemistry

questions.question: Identify the functional group responsible for the acidic properties of the given natural product.

options.explanation: Hydroxyl groups are weakly acidic, but not as acidic as carboxylic acid groups.
Ketones are not acidic.
The carboxylic acid group (–COOH) is the functional group that gives the compound its acidic properties.
Amide groups are generally neutral or weakly basic.

questions.explanation: The carboxylic acid group (–COOH) is the functional group that gives the compound its acidic properties.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the role of chlorophyll in photosynthesis?

options.text: Chlorophyll absorbs light primarily in the green region of the spectrum and reflects red and blue light.
options.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light primarily in the blue and red regions of the spectrum.

options.text: Chlorophyll is a protein that catalyzes the reduction of carbon dioxide to glucose.
options.explanation: Chlorophyll is not a protein, and it does not catalyze the reduction of carbon dioxide to glucose.

options.text: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy and converts it into chemical energy during the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis.
options.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy and converts it into chemical energy during the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis.

options.text: Chlorophyll is a pigment that is only found in the mitochondria of plant cells.
options.explanation: Chlorophyll is found in the chloroplasts of plant cells, not in the mitochondria.

questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy and converts it into chemical energy during the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which enzyme catalyzes the first committed step in the reaction pathway from glucose to pyruvic acid?

options.explanation: Hexokinase catalyzes the first step (Glucose → Glucose-6-phosphate), but this is not the committed step.
The first committed step in glycolysis is catalyzed by pyruvate kinase, which converts phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) to pyruvate.
Pyruvate dehydrogenase acts later (Pyruvic acid → Acetyl-CoA).
Rubisco is involved in the Calvin cycle, not glycolysis.

questions.explanation: The first committed step in glycolysis is catalyzed by pyruvate kinase, which converts phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) to pyruvate.

questions.question: A natural product has the molecular formula C₁₅H₂₄O₃ and contains one carboxylic acid group and two double bonds. How many rings are present in the structure?

options.explanation: The compound has at least 1 degree of unsaturation from rings.
The compound has more than 1 degree of unsaturation from rings.
The compound has 2 rings, accounting for the remaining 1 degree of unsaturation.
The compound does not have enough degrees of unsaturation to account for 3 rings.

questions.explanation: Using the degree of unsaturation formula, the compound has 4 degrees of unsaturation, with 3 degrees accounted for by the carboxylic acid group and two double bonds, leaving 1 degree for rings.
